:::{#thm-row-deriv-tp-col-deriv}
#### Row and column derivatives are transposes
$$\derivf{f(\vb)}{\tp{\vb}} = \tp{\paren{\derivf{f(\vb)}{\vb}}}$$ {#eq-row-deriv-tp-col-deriv}

$$\derivf{f(\vb)}{\vb} = \tp{\paren{\derivf{f(\vb)}{\tp{\vb}}}}$$ {#eq-col-deriv-tp-row-deriv}

:::

::: proof
By @def-vector-derivative and @def-row-vector-derivative,
entry $j$ of both $\derivf{f(\vb)}{\vb}$ and $\derivf{f(\vb)}{\tp{\vb}}$
is $\deriv{\beta_j} f(\vb)$;
the first is a $p \times 1$ column and the second a $1 \times p$ row
with the same entries in the same order,
so each is the transpose of the other.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-row-deriv-tp-col-deriv}
#### Row and column derivatives of a linear function

For $f(\vb) = 3\beta_1 + 5\beta_2$:

$$
\derivf{f(\vb)}{\vb} = \sbmat{3 \\ 5},
\qquad
\derivf{f(\vb)}{\tp{\vb}} = \sbmat{3 & 5},
$$

and each is the transpose of the other.

:::
